clue.text: New gallery housing old, symbolic work of art

indicators.note: something made new is refashioned, so the following word's letters are rearranged
housing something means giving it a home inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A newly opened gallery displays an old painting full of symbolism.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged GALLERY takes O into its middle to give ALLEGORY.
explanation.definitionFit: An allegory is a story or picture whose figures stand for hidden moral or political meanings.

clue.text: A bishop welcomed by a Buddhist monk somewhere in America

indicators.note: someone welcomed by others is taken in among them, so this pair goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
taken as written
a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk

explanation.surface: A Christian bishop is greeted warmly by a Buddhist monk on a visit to the States.
explanation.walkthrough: The welcomed pair slips in after the second letter of the monk's phrase, not at its exact centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabama is a state in the southern United States, so it is one place in America.

clue.text: Enjoyed having a relationship with no obligation, ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately points to the end, so only the final letter of the word before it is meant
with no means lacking, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: things having a relationship are connected
the final letter of obligation

explanation.surface: Someone enjoyed a no-strings romance.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a casual fling; LINKED loses its N.
explanation.definitionFit: To have liked something is to have found it pleasant, which is what enjoyed means.

clue.text: Gosh, nothing can be seen in nasty dense smog

indicators.note: nasty suggests something messed up, so the following letters are jumbled
something seen in a thing is inside it, so this piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that nothing is visible through thick smog.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodness me and gosh are both mild exclamations of surprise.

clue.text: Dried fruit is placed in water

indicators.note: placed in means put inside, so the short word goes within the other

blocks.note: rain is water falling from the sky
taken as written

explanation.surface: Dried fruit is soaked in water to plump it up.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a dried grape, a common dried fruit.

clue.text: Jazz tune accompanying a sitar melody

blocks.note: a rag is a piece of ragtime music
taken as written

explanation.surface: A jazz number is played alongside a sitar melody, a fusion gig.
explanation.definitionFit: A raga is a traditional melodic framework of Indian classical music, often played on the sitar.

clue.text: Devoted group supporting a party

blocks.note: taken as written
a do is a party
a ring is a group of people, as in a spy ring

explanation.surface: Loyal members back a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: Party reads as a political party, but it is a social do.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoring means showing deep love and devotion, as devoted does.

clue.text: Active US soldier involved in sallies from time to time

indicators.note: from time to time means only now and then, so every other letter is used
involved in means caught up inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the even-placed letters of sallies
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: An energetic American soldier occasionally takes part in sorties.
explanation.walkthrough: A sally is a sudden charge out from a defended position, which suits the soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Agile means nimble and quick-moving, so it describes someone active.

clue.text: Demand technical support and invite trouble

blocks.note: a two-word phrasal verb meaning to request something
IT, information technology, is the office technical-support department

explanation.surface: Someone demanding help from tech support is told they're courting trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask for it is an idiom for behaving in a way that provokes the punishment or trouble that follows.

clue.text: Religious festival held by Catholics

indicators.note: something held by a word sits inside it, so the answer lies within the next word

blocks.note: the letters sit in the middle of this word

explanation.surface: A religious festival is celebrated by Catholics.
explanation.walkthrough: Catholics suggests a Christian feast, but the festival is the Hindu one hidden inside the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Holi is the Hindu spring festival of colours, marked by throwing coloured powder.

clue.text: I crashed an unusually old carriage

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A driver confesses to crashing an unusually old vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: Crashed suggests a car, but the carriage is carried by people.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedan chair was an enclosed seat carried on poles by two bearers, a historical form of conveyance.

clue.text: Extra source of debts taken on by ace crime boss

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it begins, so only its opening letter is used
something taken on is absorbed into a group, so it goes inside the other pieces

blocks.note: A is the card abbreviation for ace
the opening letter of debts
a don is a Mafia boss

explanation.surface: An ace and a Mafia boss pile on debts as an extra charge.
explanation.walkthrough: D goes inside A plus DON.
explanation.definitionFit: An add-on is a supplementary item or charge attached to something already bought.

clue.text: Retrospective pieces from magazines I meticulously catalogue

indicators.note: pieces taken from words are fragments of them, so the answer lies across them
a retrospective looks back, so the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of magazines, I and the start of meticulously

explanation.surface: I carefully catalogue retrospective articles from old magazines.
explanation.walkthrough: Retrospective reads like a description of the pieces, an art-show or look-back feature, but it tells you to read the hidden letters backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To itemise is to list things one by one, which is what cataloguing does.

clue.text: Stupid people start to slander judge

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which is all that is used

blocks.note: asses are fools
the opening letter of slander

explanation.surface: Foolish people begin badmouthing a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: Judge looks like the target of the slander, but it is the definition, used as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess something is to evaluate it, which is what judging means as a verb.

clue.text: Small watch? It might be tacky

blocks.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
ticker is slang for a watch

explanation.surface: Someone eyes a little wristwatch and wonders if it is in poor taste.
explanation.walkthrough: Tacky looks like a verdict on the watch's taste; it means sticky.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticker is an adhesive label, and tacky also means slightly sticky to the touch.

clue.text: After noon, attempt to enter bar? Exactly!

indicators.note: after places the next piece behind the one named first, fixing their order
to enter something is to go inside it, so this pair goes within the next piece

blocks.note: to bar is to ban
N is short for noon
a go is an attempt

explanation.surface: Someone tries to get into the pub after midday, and is praised for good timing.
explanation.walkthrough: Bar looks like a pub, but it is the verb meaning prohibit; the noon-plus-attempt pair sits just before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Bang on is informal British praise meaning precisely right or spot on.

clue.text: Simple tea's now being prepared

indicators.note: something being prepared is being made up, so the letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Making a cup of tea is an easy job, and it's on its way.
explanation.definitionFit: No sweat is an informal phrase meaning no trouble, said of a task that is easy.

clue.text: A piece of cake or French cheeses picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: Brie is a soft French cheese

explanation.surface: A slice of cake or some French cheeses are collected from a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: A piece of cake sits beside cheeses as food, but it is the idiom for something easy.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeze is informal for an easy task, and a piece of cake is an idiom with the same sense.

clue.text: Cook slowly eats the last portion of raw fish?

indicators.note: whatever eats something takes it inside, so one piece swallows the other
the last portion of a word is its final letter, which is all that is kept

blocks.note: to simmer is to cook gently just below the boil
the final letter of raw

explanation.walkthrough: Fish looks like the food being cooked; with its question mark it defines something that swims, a fish being one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish is an example of a creature that moves through water, hence a swimmer, signalled by the question mark.

clue.text: Lets go of instrument in audition

blocks.note: a sax is a saxophone

explanation.surface: A band leader drops a musician's instrument at the try-out.
explanation.walkthrough: Audition suggests a musician's tryout, which matches the sacking, but it means a hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack someone is to dismiss them from a job, which is letting them go.

clue.text: Firms with extremely tenuous charges

the first and last letters of tenuous

explanation.definitionFit: Costs are the prices or fees charged for something, so charges is a plural noun synonym.

clue.text: One in flight crossing east, costing a lot

blocks.note: a flight of stairs is made up of steps
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A single eastbound flight is expensive.
explanation.walkthrough: Flight suggests air travel, but it is a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Steep is informal for excessively expensive, as in a steep price.

clue.text: Compressed mass, oddly chalkier

indicators.note: oddly points to the odd-numbered positions, so the first, third, fifth and seventh letters are used

blocks.note: the odd-placed letters of chalkier

explanation.surface: A packed lump of something is oddly more chalky than expected.
explanation.definitionFit: A cake can be a block of compacted material, as in a cake of soap or of dried mud.

clue.text: Mountain dweller seen possibly carrying wooden stake

a pale is a pointed wooden stake, as in a fence

explanation.walkthrough: A pale is a fence post, the source of the phrase beyond the pale.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nepalese person lives in Nepal, the Himalayan country that contains Everest, so is a mountain dweller.

clue.text: Kind person

blocks.note: first meaning: a type or variety
second meaning: an individual

explanation.walkthrough: Kind reads as an adjective praising the person, but it is a noun meaning type.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a category of thing and, informally, an individual of a given character, as in a decent sort.

clue.text: Weakened pet cried out
